anti_pattern: Do not waste energy on minor blocking or inefficient attacks on turn 1 when you have Bash available and can afford the HP loss.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you are at very low HP (<20%) or facing an enemy that punishes debuffs (e.g., by cleansing or gaining strength).

trigger: When Seapunk is Vulnerable and you have sufficient block to fully absorb its attack
lesson: When Seapunk is Vulnerable and you have enough block to cover its damage, maximize damage output by playing high-damage cards like Dismantle first, then finishing with Strikes, rather than over-blocking or playing inefficient cards.
recommendation: Play Dismantle (or other high-damage cards) while Vulnerable is active, then follow with Strikes to finish the fight, as the damage multiplier makes these plays highly efficient.
anti_pattern: Do not play additional block cards or low-damage attacks when you already have sufficient block and can kill the enemy within the Vulnerable window.
counterfactual: Do not apply if Seapunk is not Vulnerable or if you cannot kill it this turn (save damage for next turn instead).

trigger: When facing Living Fog with high HP and a Vulnerable-applying card (Bash) plus a multi-hit card (Dismantle) in hand
lesson: Against Living Fog, prioritize applying Vulnerable before playing multi-hit attacks to maximize damage output, even when the enemy's attack is small and survivable.
recommendation: Play Bash first to apply Vulnerable, then follow with Dismantle (or other multi-hit attacks) to double the damage from the Vulnerable multiplier.
anti_pattern: Playing Dismantle before Bash, or ending the turn without using the Vulnerable window, wastes significant damage potential.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the enemy has high block or if you need to block a lethal attack this turn.

trigger: When deciding whether to block against Living Fog's small attacks while at high HP
lesson: Against Living Fog's low-damage attacks (5-8 damage), it is safe to forgo blocking when HP is high (above 75%) and Burning Blood provides passive healing.
recommendation: Accept small damage from Living Fog to conserve block cards and potions for more threatening encounters, relying on Burning Blood to recover.
anti_pattern: Using block potions or playing block cards against Living Fog's small attacks when HP is high wastes resources.
counterfactual: Do not apply if HP is low (below 50%) or if the enemy is about to enter a more dangerous phase.

trigger: When facing Gas Bomb with a Strike or 6+ damage attack and it is Vulnerable
lesson: A single Strike (6 base + 50% Vulnerable = 9) kills a full-health Gas Bomb (7 HP) in Act 1, preventing its 8-damage attack.
recommendation: Prioritize killing Gas Bomb with a Strike if Vulnerable is applied, even if it means overkilling slightly, to avoid its attack.
anti_pattern: Wasting a higher-damage card or multi-hit attack on Gas Bomb when a Strike would suffice.
counterfactual: Not applicable if Gas Bomb has block or if you lack Vulnerable and cannot reach 7 damage with a single card.

trigger: When facing Living Fog with a minion that can be killed this turn and you have Iron Wave in hand
lesson: Iron Wave can serve as a finisher for a low-HP minion while simultaneously generating block against the remaining enemy's incoming attack.
recommendation: Use Iron Wave to finish a nearly-dead minion to gain block for the next enemy's attack, rather than using a pure block card or a different attack.
anti_pattern: Using a separate block card (e.g., Shrug It Off) and a different attack card when Iron Wave can accomplish both tasks in one card play.
counterfactual: Not optimal if the minion has more HP than Iron Wave can deal, or if you need the draw from Shrug It Off more than the block.

trigger: When facing Living Fog with Smoggy active and have a Bash in hand
lesson: Bash is worth playing even when taking 5 damage from Smoggy because Vulnerable doubles subsequent Strike damage, making the trade efficient.
recommendation: Play Bash early in the turn to apply Vulnerable, then follow with Strikes to maximize damage output before the debuff expires.
anti_pattern: Avoid skipping Bash due to Smoggy self-damage when you have Strikes to follow up.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you lack follow-up attacks or if your HP is critically low.

trigger: When Living Fog is at very low HP and you cannot kill this turn
lesson: Ending turn without blocking is acceptable when the enemy's incoming damage is small (5) and you have full energy next turn to finish it.
recommendation: Accept the small damage and end turn to set up a lethal next turn rather than wasting block cards.
anti_pattern: Do not waste block cards or energy on unnecessary defense when the enemy is nearly dead and deals minimal damage.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the enemy's attack is large enough to threaten lethal or if you have no guaranteed lethal next turn.

trigger: When facing multiple Phantasmal Gardeners with Skittish active
lesson: Against Skittish, prioritize breaking the block on one enemy at a time with cheap attacks before committing high-damage attacks, to avoid wasting damage on the block gain.
recommendation: Use a low-cost attack (Strike, Iron Wave) first to break Skittish on a target, then follow up with higher-damage attacks on the same enemy to deal real HP damage.
anti_pattern: Playing a high-damage attack first against a Skittish enemy, which wastes damage on the block gain.
counterfactual: If you have enough damage to kill through Skittish in one hit, or if the enemy has no Skittish, this sequencing is unnecessary.

trigger: When deciding whether to use a block potion against multiple Phantasmal Gardeners
lesson: Block Potion is worth using to prevent significant damage when hand is empty and incoming damage exceeds current block by a meaningful margin (e.g., 9+ HP saved).
recommendation: Use Block Potion when you have empty hand and incoming damage exceeds your block by at least 9 HP, to preserve HP for the rest of the fight.
anti_pattern: Hoarding potions too aggressively and taking avoidable damage that could have been prevented with a potion.
counterfactual: If you have strong block cards in hand or can end the fight soon, saving the potion may be better.

trigger: When facing multiple Phantasmal Gardeners with Skittish block and you have a multi-hit attack (e.g., One-Two Punch + Dismantle) in hand
lesson: Against Phantasmal Gardener, prioritize removing one enemy per turn to reduce incoming damage. Use a cheap attack first to break Skittish block, then follow up with multi-hit attacks to kill. This is better than spreading damage or playing full block.
recommendation: Sequence: cheap attack to break block -> multi-hit attack to kill -> remaining energy for block. This maximizes damage output while minimizing incoming damage.
anti_pattern: Don't play block first against Skittish enemies; you waste the block when they attack through it, and you miss the chance to remove an attacker.
counterfactual: Not applicable if you cannot kill any enemy this turn; then full block is better.

trigger: When you have Flame Barrier and enemies are attacking for more than 12 damage total
lesson: Flame Barrier alone is often the best play against multiple Phantasmal Gardeners: it blocks 12 damage, deals 8 retaliation damage (4 per attack), and leaves energy for other plays. This is better than full blocking (wastes energy) or ignoring block (takes too much damage).
recommendation: Play Flame Barrier when facing 2+ attackers dealing 16+ total damage. It provides efficient block + counter-damage. Use remaining energy to break Skittish block on a priority target.
anti_pattern: Don't over-block with extra Defends when Flame Barrier already covers most damage; use remaining energy to set up kills instead.
counterfactual: Not optimal if enemies are not attacking this turn, or if you can kill an enemy and reduce incoming damage to 0.

trigger: When facing Phantasmal Gardener with Skittish block and considering whether to attack through block
lesson: Against Phantasmal Gardener's Skittish (block on attack), it can be correct to attack through the block if the damage is sufficient for lethal, even if some damage is wasted on block.
recommendation: Calculate if post-block damage kills the enemy; if yes, attack through Skittish to remove the threat rather than waiting for the block to decay.
anti_pattern: Avoiding all attacks because of Skittish block, delaying lethal and taking extra turns of damage.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the attack cannot kill through the block and you have alternative ways to remove the block (e.g., multi-hit attacks).

trigger: When deciding whether to play all block cards or save energy for next turn with no attacks in hand
lesson: With no attacks in hand against Phantasmal Gardener, it is often better to save some energy for next turn rather than over-blocking, since the enemy's damage is predictable and you can afford to take some chip damage.
recommendation: If you have no attacks in hand, calculate the minimum block needed to survive and save remaining energy for next turn's offense.
anti_pattern: Playing all block cards to zero energy when you have no attacks, wasting energy that could be used for lethal next turn.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you are at critical HP where any chip damage risks death, or if the enemy has an unpredictable attack pattern.

trigger: When facing Phantasmal Gardener with a multi-hit attack plan and the enemy has Skittish block
lesson: Against Phantasmal Gardener's Skittish, sequence cheap attacks first to strip block before playing high-damage cards. This maximizes net HP damage per turn.
recommendation: Play a low-cost attack (Strike, 1-cost) before a high-damage card (Dismantle, 2-cost) to break Skittish block first, ensuring the high-damage card deals full HP damage.
anti_pattern: Playing a high-damage card first against Skittish wastes its damage on block, reducing effective damage output.
counterfactual: Not applicable if the enemy does not have Skittish or if you have a single attack that can break block and deal damage in one hit.

trigger: When considering Bloodletting against Phantasmal Gardener on a non-attack turn
lesson: Bloodletting is safe and valuable on non-attack turns against Phantasmal Gardener, as the 3 HP cost is minor compared to the energy gain for next turn's burst.
recommendation: Play Bloodletting on turns when the enemy is buffing or not attacking to bank energy for a stronger follow-up turn, even if it costs a few HP.
anti_pattern: Avoiding Bloodletting due to HP loss on non-attack turns, missing out on energy for lethal or block setups.
counterfactual: Not recommended if HP is critically low (below 10) or if the enemy's next attack is lethal and you cannot block.

trigger: When facing Skulking Colony with a Flame Barrier in hand and the enemy has low HP (≤ 4) and is about to attack
lesson: Flame Barrier's thorns damage can secure lethal against Skulking Colony even when the card's direct damage is capped by Hardened Shell, as thorns damage bypasses the cap.
recommendation: When Skulking Colony has ≤ 4 HP and is attacking, play Flame Barrier for block + thorns lethal instead of attacking directly, to avoid taking unnecessary damage.
anti_pattern: Playing a direct attack card when Flame Barrier thorns would kill the enemy, taking unnecessary damage.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the enemy is not attacking this turn, or if you need to preserve Flame Barrier for a future turn.

trigger: When deciding whether to block or attack against Skulking Colony with high HP and the damage cap is in effect
lesson: Against Skulking Colony, it is often correct to accept moderate damage (e.g., 8-14 HP) in order to maximize damage output within the 15-damage cap per card, rather than over-blocking and prolonging the fight.
recommendation: When HP is comfortable (≥ 60% max HP) and you have damage cards that hit the cap, prioritize dealing damage over full blocking, even if it means taking 8-14 damage. The fight ends faster, reducing total damage taken.
anti_pattern: Over-blocking and dealing minimal damage, causing the fight to drag on and accumulate more damage over multiple turns.
counterfactual: Do not apply if HP is low (≤ 40% max HP) or if the enemy is about to use a very high-damage attack (> 20).

trigger: When facing Calcified Cultist + Damp Cultist on turn 1 with Bloodletting, Inflame, and Dismantle in hand
lesson: Against non-attacking turn 1 enemies, prioritize setting up Strength with Bloodletting + Inflame before using Dismantle to maximize damage output
recommendation: Play Bloodletting first for energy, then Inflame for Strength, then Dismantle the higher-priority target (Calcified Cultist) for lethal or near-lethal damage
anti_pattern: Don't play Dismantle before Strength buffs, as it wastes damage potential
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemies attack on turn 1 or if you lack sufficient block

trigger: When Calcified Cultist is at very low HP (6 or less) and both enemies are buffing (non-attacking)
lesson: Using Gambler's Brew to fish for lethal on a low-HP non-attacking enemy is a good risk-reward trade when the alternative is letting it survive to attack next turn
recommendation: Use Gambler's Brew to redraw for lethal damage when enemies are not attacking and a key threat is nearly dead
anti_pattern: Don't waste Gambler's Brew when enemies are attacking and you need block cards instead
counterfactual: Not worth it if you already have lethal in hand or if the potion is needed for a harder fight soon

trigger: when facing multiple enemies and Thunderclap is in hand and can kill one enemy
lesson: Thunderclap is a high-value AoE attack that applies Vulnerable; prioritize it over single-target attacks when it can secure a kill on one enemy while damaging others.
recommendation: Play Thunderclap if it can kill at least one enemy and damage another, even if a single-target attack would also kill the primary target.
anti_pattern: Playing a single-target attack (e.g., Strike) when Thunderclap can kill one enemy and damage the other, wasting the AoE and debuff potential.
counterfactual: Do not play Thunderclap if it would leave both enemies alive with no follow-up to finish them, or if energy is needed for block.

trigger: when facing Damp Cultist and it is not attacking this turn
lesson: Prioritize dealing damage over blocking when the Cultist is not attacking, as it only scales when attacking.
recommendation: Use attacks aggressively on turns the Cultist is not attacking to race its scaling.
anti_pattern: Playing block cards or defensive skills when the enemy is not attacking and you have lethal or near-lethal damage.
counterfactual: Not applicable if the Cultist is attacking and you lack sufficient HP to tank the hit.

trigger: when calculating lethal damage against Damp Cultist with Vulnerable applied
lesson: Account for Vulnerable multiplier when calculating lethal damage thresholds to avoid overkill or missed lethal.
recommendation: When the Cultist has Vulnerable, multiply base damage by 1.5 to determine if a card is lethal.
anti_pattern: Using a high-damage card like Bash when a cheaper Strike would be lethal due to Vulnerable.
counterfactual: Not applicable if the enemy is not Vulnerable or if you need to apply Vulnerable for future turns.

trigger: When facing multiple Corpse Slugs and you have a scaling power (e.g., Inflame) in hand
lesson: Prioritize playing scaling powers early against Corpse Slugs even when taking significant damage, because the fight snowballs once you kill one (Ravenous stuns others).
recommendation: Play Inflame (or similar scaling) on turn 1 even if you take full damage, as the strength boost accelerates kills and prevents future damage via stuns.
anti_pattern: Playing Defend or delaying scaling to mitigate early damage, which prolongs the fight and leads to more total damage taken.
counterfactual: Not applicable if you have lethal on a Slug this turn or if your HP is critically low (<20%).

trigger: When you have a draw card (e.g., Vicious) and an enemy is low enough to kill with a drawn attack
lesson: Use draw cards to fish for lethal on a low-HP Corpse Slug, as killing one stuns all others and ends the threat.
recommendation: Play Vicious (or similar draw) before committing to block, as drawing an attack can kill the low Slug and make blocking unnecessary.
anti_pattern: Playing Defend first and missing the chance to draw into lethal, taking unnecessary damage.
counterfactual: Not applicable if you have no attacks in deck that can finish the low enemy, or if the drawn card would leave you unable to block lethal damage.

trigger: When facing multiple Corpse Slugs and one is low enough to kill with available damage
lesson: Killing one Corpse Slug stuns the other, preventing its debuff and attacks for a turn, which can be more valuable than splitting damage.
recommendation: Focus damage to kill one Slug at a time rather than spreading damage evenly, to trigger the stun mechanic and reduce incoming damage.
anti_pattern: Splitting damage evenly between two Corpse Slugs, which delays the stun and allows both to attack/debuff.
counterfactual: Not applicable if you cannot kill a Slug this turn, or if the other Slug is already stunned.

trigger: When Corpse Slug is stunned and you have a card that provides permanent scaling (e.g., Plating) and only 1 energy
lesson: Prioritize permanent scaling over immediate block when the enemy is stunned and cannot attack
recommendation: Play the permanent scaling card (e.g., Stone Armor) even if it consumes all energy, as the future block generation outweighs the temporary block loss
anti_pattern: Holding energy for a future attack when the scaling card is available and the enemy is stunned
counterfactual: Do not apply if the enemy is not stunned and will attack next turn, or if the scaling card is low-impact

trigger: When calculating lethal damage against Corpse Slug with a multi-hit attack that has strength scaling
lesson: Multi-hit attacks with strength scaling can overkill Corpse Slug; verify exact damage to avoid wasting energy on unnecessary follow-up attacks
recommendation: Calculate total damage from multi-hit attacks (including strength bonuses) before playing additional cards; if lethal, end turn to conserve energy
anti_pattern: Playing a second attack after a multi-hit attack already achieved lethal, wasting energy
counterfactual: Do not apply if the multi-hit attack does not guarantee lethal or if the enemy has block/intangibility

trigger: When facing Lagavulin Matriarch with low HP and the enemy is about to attack for lethal, and you have a Flame Barrier in hand.
lesson: Flame Barrier is a high-priority survival tool against Lagavulin Matriarch's big attacks; do not waste it on small block when you can use it to survive a lethal hit and deal damage back.
recommendation: Prioritize playing Flame Barrier when it exactly blocks lethal damage, even if it means not playing attacks that turn. The reflected damage and survival are more valuable than a few extra points of damage.
anti_pattern: Playing attacks instead of Flame Barrier when you are at low HP and the enemy is attacking for lethal, leaving you dead next turn.
counterfactual: If you have enough block from other sources to survive the attack, or if you can kill the enemy this turn, then Flame Barrier may not be the priority.

trigger: When facing Lagavulin Matriarch and you have Bloodletting in hand with high HP.
lesson: Bloodletting is a strong energy generator early in the Lagavulin fight when you have high HP, enabling more attacks per turn to race the enemy's scaling.
recommendation: Play Bloodletting early (turn 2 or 3) when you have high HP (above 75%) to convert HP into energy for a burst damage turn. This accelerates the fight and reduces the number of turns you need to survive.
anti_pattern: Hesitating to play Bloodletting due to HP loss, leading to slower damage output and more turns of taking big hits.
counterfactual: If your HP is low (below 50%) or you lack high-damage cards to spend the energy on, Bloodletting may be too risky.

trigger: when facing two Corpse Slugs and one has been weakened or has taken damage
lesson: Killing one Corpse Slug stuns the other, preventing its attack for the turn.
recommendation: Prioritize killing one Corpse Slug over splitting damage, even if it requires using a high-damage card like Dismantle, to stun the other and avoid incoming damage.
anti_pattern: Splitting damage evenly between both slugs, allowing both to attack.
counterfactual: Not applicable if you cannot kill a slug this turn or if both are at full HP and you lack lethal damage.

trigger: when you have a permanent stat-boosting potion (e.g., Fysh Oil) and are safe from taking damage this turn
lesson: Using a permanent stat-boosting potion early in combat maximizes its value over the fight.
recommendation: Use Fysh Oil (or similar) on a turn where you have sufficient block or are otherwise safe, to gain the +1 Str and +1 Dex for the remainder of the fight.
anti_pattern: Holding the potion indefinitely or using it on a turn where you take damage unnecessarily.
counterfactual: Do not use if you need the potion slot for a more urgent potion, or if the fight is nearly over.

trigger: enemy is stunned and current hand cannot kill this turn
lesson: When enemy is stunned and hand damage is insufficient to kill, using Gambler's Brew to redraw for lethal is a high-value play that avoids taking unnecessary damage next turn.
recommendation: If enemy is stunned and you have lethal potential in deck but not in hand, use Gambler's Brew to fish for kill. Only do this if you have enough energy to play the new cards.
anti_pattern: Holding Gambler's Brew for later when a guaranteed stun turn offers a safe window to redraw for lethal.
counterfactual: Do not use if you already have lethal in hand, or if enemy is not stunned and will attack next turn (risk of wasting potion without improving survival).

trigger: enemy is stunned and you have attack cards in hand
lesson: When the enemy is stunned, prioritize dealing damage over playing block cards, even if the block card also deals damage.
recommendation: Play pure attack cards first; if you must play a hybrid card like Iron Wave, accept that the block portion is wasted but the damage is still valuable.
anti_pattern: Playing a block card for its block value when the enemy is stunned and cannot attack.
counterfactual: If the enemy is not stunned and will attack next turn, block may be necessary.

trigger: enemy HP is low enough to kill with two attacks and you have enough energy
lesson: Against Corpse Slug, sequence high-damage cards first (e.g., Dismantle for 9) then follow with a Strike to finish, minimizing wasted overkill.
recommendation: Play the highest-damage-per-energy card first, then the next highest, to avoid overkill and end the fight efficiently.
anti_pattern: Playing a low-damage card first when a high-damage card could kill or set up a clean kill.
counterfactual: If the enemy has high HP and you cannot kill this turn, consider setting up for future turns instead.

trigger: when facing multiple Toadpoles and one is attacking for small damage (<=7) while you have high HP (>75%)
lesson: Prioritize damaging the attacking Toadpole over blocking when HP is high, as the damage is acceptable and accelerates kill.
recommendation: Play highest damage card on the attacking Toadpole first, then use remaining energy for block or further damage.
anti_pattern: Blocking fully with Defend(s) when you could instead deal damage and take small chip damage, wasting damage potential.
counterfactual: Do not apply if enemy attack is large (>=15) or your HP is low (<50%).

trigger: when you have Iron Wave and Strike in hand against a low-HP Toadpole (<=9 HP) that is attacking
lesson: Sequence Iron Wave before Strike to gain block while dealing damage, then finish with Strike to kill, minimizing incoming damage.
recommendation: Play Iron Wave first for damage+block, then Strike to kill, then use remaining energy for Defend if needed.
anti_pattern: Playing Strike first and then Iron Wave, missing the block from Iron Wave and taking unnecessary damage.
counterfactual: Do not apply if Iron Wave would overkill or if you need to save energy for a different play.

trigger: when enemy is at very low HP (<=7) and you have lethal damage in hand with a Strike or basic attack
lesson: Prioritize finishing the fight with the cheapest lethal attack rather than overkilling or playing block, even if enemy will attack next turn.
recommendation: When enemy HP is low enough to die to a single Strike (6 damage), play that Strike immediately to end combat and avoid unnecessary damage.
anti_pattern: Playing a more expensive attack (e.g., Perfected Strike for 18) when a cheaper Strike would also kill, wasting energy and potentially leaving you unable to block.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy has Thorns or if you need to set up a combo for a harder fight later.

trigger: when you have exactly 1 energy remaining after playing a big attack and enemy will deal lethal or near-lethal damage next turn
lesson: If you cannot fully block incoming damage with remaining energy, it is often better to deal as much damage as possible to shorten the fight rather than playing a partial block.
recommendation: With 1 energy and enemy at 7 HP, play a Strike to kill instead of playing Defend to block 5 and take 2+Thorns damage, which prolongs the fight.
anti_pattern: Playing a block card for partial mitigation when you could instead kill the enemy and end the fight entirely.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy has multiple attackers or if you have a strong block card that fully negates damage.

trigger: when facing Seapunk with high HP and Stomp in hand
lesson: Against Seapunk, sequence attacks to maximize Stomp's damage reduction: play attacks first to lower Stomp's cost, then play Stomp for efficient burst.
recommendation: Play cheap attacks (Strike, Dismantle) before Stomp to reduce its cost to 1 energy, then use remaining energy on Stomp for high damage output.
anti_pattern: Playing Stomp early when it costs 2 energy, wasting damage potential.
counterfactual: Do not apply if Stomp is already free (cost 0) or if you lack energy to follow up with other attacks.

trigger: when at 0 energy with no playable cards and a potion available
lesson: Using a potion to generate a free action is better than ending turn and taking full damage, even if the potion's effect is uncertain.
recommendation: When out of energy and hand is unplayable, use a potion (e.g., Skill Potion) to create an extra action rather than passing turn.
anti_pattern: Hoarding potions when they could prevent damage or accelerate kills.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the potion is critical for a future elite/boss fight and current damage is negligible.

trigger: when enemy is about to attack for exactly the amount of block you have and you cannot kill it this turn
lesson: If you have exactly enough block to fully absorb the enemy's attack and cannot kill the enemy this turn, end turn to preserve cards and energy for a stronger next turn.
recommendation: Calculate whether you can kill the enemy this turn. If not, and you have sufficient block to survive, end turn rather than playing inefficient attacks.
anti_pattern: Playing weak attacks that don't kill when you already have enough block to survive, wasting cards and energy.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you can kill the enemy this turn, or if the enemy's attack is variable and might exceed your block.

trigger: when you have a high-damage attack and a finisher in hand with enough energy to play both
lesson: Against Seapunk (45 HP), sequence high-damage attacks first to maximize the chance of killing before needing to block, as Seapunk's damage output is moderate.
recommendation: Play your highest damage card first (e.g., Perfected Strike for 18), then follow up with a finisher (e.g., Dismantle for 8) to kill efficiently.
anti_pattern: Playing block cards or low-damage attacks first when you have lethal damage in hand, giving the enemy an extra turn.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the enemy has high damage output that turn and you need to block first to survive.

trigger: when facing Living Fog with Bash and Dismantle in hand on first turn
lesson: Against Living Fog, playing Bash first to apply Vulnerable enables Dismantle to deal 24 damage on the same turn, maximizing burst damage before the enemy's Smoggy restriction limits skill usage.
recommendation: Play Bash before Dismantle on turn 1 to apply Vulnerable and maximize Dismantle's damage output in a single turn.
anti_pattern: Playing Dismantle first without Vulnerable, or delaying Bash to a later turn, reduces burst damage and wastes the Vulnerable window.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the enemy is not Living Fog or if Dismantle is not in hand.

trigger: when Living Fog's Smoggy restricts skill usage and current block exactly matches incoming attack
lesson: Against Living Fog with Smoggy active, if current block exactly equals the enemy's attack, ending turn is optimal to avoid wasting energy and cards on overblocking.
recommendation: End turn when block exactly matches incoming damage, rather than playing extra block cards that would be wasted.
anti_pattern: Playing a Defend or other block card when block already covers the incoming attack, wasting energy and a card draw.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the enemy has multiple attacks or if block is insufficient to cover all incoming damage.

trigger: when facing Gas Bomb and Living Fog with a multi-target attack (e.g., Stomp) in hand
lesson: Prioritize killing Gas Bomb first to prevent its DeathBlow, then use a multi-target attack to damage both enemies efficiently.
recommendation: Play single-target attacks on Gas Bomb until it is dead, then use multi-target attacks to damage both enemies.
anti_pattern: Using multi-target attack before killing Gas Bomb, leaving it alive to use DeathBlow.
counterfactual: If you have enough block to survive DeathBlow or can kill both in one multi-target attack, this order may not be optimal.

trigger: when enemy HP is low enough to be killed by a single attack and you have block from a previous card play
lesson: When enemy is at lethal HP, prioritize playing a block-generating attack first if it fully mitigates incoming damage, then finish with a higher-damage attack. This sequence avoids taking damage while securing the kill.
recommendation: Order attacks to maximize block before lethal: play a block+damage card first if it covers all incoming damage, then use the remaining energy for the killing blow.
anti_pattern: Playing the lethal attack first and wasting block potential, taking unnecessary damage.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the block card does not fully block incoming damage or if the enemy has a multi-hit attack that would bypass partial block.

trigger: when facing multiple enemies with block-gaining attacks and you have a Perfected Strike
lesson: Prioritize focusing damage on one enemy to remove it quickly, even if it means overkilling its block, rather than splitting damage across both enemies.
recommendation: When you have a high-damage single-target attack like Perfected Strike and one enemy has gained block, still target the same enemy to remove it from combat faster, reducing future incoming damage.
anti_pattern: Splitting damage across both enemies or switching targets because the primary target gained block.
counterfactual: If both enemies have lethal next turn or you have AoE that kills both, splitting may be better.

trigger: when you have a Colorless Potion and are deciding whether to use it during combat
lesson: Use Colorless Potion early in a turn when you have remaining energy to play the generated card, not at the end of a turn when you cannot use the card.
recommendation: If you have energy remaining and the potion could provide a useful card, use it before playing other cards to maximize the chance of using the generated card that same turn.
anti_pattern: Using Colorless Potion at the end of a turn when you have no energy left, wasting the potential of the free card.
counterfactual: If you have no energy remaining or the potion is better saved for a future more critical turn, do not use it.

trigger: when facing multiple Punch Constructs and one is low HP
lesson: Prioritize killing a low-HP Punch Construct to reduce incoming damage, even if it means overkilling slightly.
recommendation: Use a cheap attack (e.g., Headbutt) to finish off a nearly dead Punch Construct, then use remaining energy to block or damage the other.
anti_pattern: Saving a high-damage card for later when a cheap attack can secure the kill now.
counterfactual: If the low-HP enemy has block or intangible, consider other sequencing.

trigger: when facing multiple Punch Constructs and you have no block in hand
lesson: Accepting moderate damage (e.g., 14 HP) to kill one enemy quickly is often correct, as it reduces future damage.
recommendation: If you can kill or nearly kill one Punch Construct this turn, take the damage rather than playing a weak block card.
anti_pattern: Playing a weak block card (e.g., 5 block) when you could instead deal lethal damage to one enemy.
counterfactual: If your HP is very low (below 20% max), prioritize blocking.

trigger: when facing Punch Construct with low HP and an attack-heavy hand
lesson: Use Bash to strip block and apply Vulnerable before playing multi-hit attacks like Dismantle to maximize damage per energy, even if it delays lethal by a turn.
recommendation: Play Bash first to remove block and apply Vulnerable, then follow with Dismantle for double damage. This sequence can set up a kill next turn even if you take damage.
anti_pattern: Playing Dismantle before Bash when enemy has block, wasting damage potential.
counterfactual: Do not apply if enemy has no block or if you can kill this turn without Vulnerable.

trigger: when at very low HP (below 10) and enemy is about to attack for lethal
lesson: When low HP and enemy will attack for lethal next turn, prioritize finishing the fight this turn even if it means using all energy on damage, as Burning Blood can heal you post-combat.
recommendation: If you have enough damage to kill, play all damage cards immediately. Do not hold back energy for block if death is guaranteed next turn.
anti_pattern: Saving energy or playing block when you could kill, risking death from the incoming attack.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you cannot kill this turn; then block is necessary.

trigger: both enemies are buffing on their first turn
lesson: When both enemies are buffing and not attacking, maximize damage output without regard for block, even if it means spending all energy.
recommendation: Use all energy on attacks when no enemy will deal damage this turn. Prioritize bringing the lower-HP enemy close to lethal to reduce future incoming damage.
anti_pattern: Playing block cards or saving energy when enemies are not attacking, which delays kills and prolongs the fight.
counterfactual: Not applicable if any enemy is attacking this turn.

trigger: Calcified Cultist is at very low HP (4 or less) and you have an attack that exhausts
lesson: Use an exhausting attack to finish a low-HP enemy, thinning the deck for future turns while conserving higher-damage cards.
recommendation: Prefer using cards that exhaust (e.g., Molten Fist) to secure the kill on a nearly-dead enemy, as it removes itself from the deck and frees up draws for better cards.
anti_pattern: Using a non-exhausting high-damage card (e.g., Perfected Strike) to finish a low-HP enemy, wasting its potential for later turns.
counterfactual: Not applicable if the exhausting card is needed for a larger threat later in the fight.

trigger: when facing Damp Cultist with low HP and a Strength potion available
lesson: Using a Strength potion early against Damp Cultist is high-value because the enemy's Ritual ability scales its damage each turn, so front-loaded damage reduces future risk.
recommendation: Use Strength potion on turn 1 against Damp Cultist to maximize damage output before the enemy's Strength scaling becomes dangerous.
anti_pattern: Saving the Strength potion for later turns when the enemy's Strength has already scaled, reducing its relative impact.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the potion is needed for a more threatening upcoming elite or boss fight.

trigger: when facing Damp Cultist with low HP and Burning Blood relic
lesson: Taking damage to play Stomp for maximum damage is acceptable when Burning Blood will heal 6 HP post-combat, effectively reducing the net HP loss.
recommendation: Prioritize high-damage attacks like Stomp even if it means taking damage, as Burning Blood offsets the HP loss and the enemy's Strength scaling makes delaying dangerous.
anti_pattern: Playing defensively (e.g., blocking) when the enemy's Strength is scaling, leading to prolonged combat and more damage taken overall.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the player has no healing relic or if the damage taken would lead to death before the next heal opportunity.

trigger: when facing multiple low-HP enemies and you cannot kill any this turn
lesson: Focus damage on one enemy to set up a kill next turn rather than spreading damage or over-blocking.
recommendation: Concentrate all attacks on the lowest-HP enemy to create a kill window next turn, even if it means taking some damage this turn.

trigger: when you have Burning Blood and are at low HP (below 25%) but can survive the turn
lesson: Accepting damage to set up a kill is safe when Burning Blood will heal you after combat.
recommendation: Trade HP for damage setup if you can survive the turn and Burning Blood will restore HP post-combat.
anti_pattern: Over-blocking at low HP when you have Burning Blood, wasting damage potential.
counterfactual: Not applicable without Burning Blood or if the incoming damage would kill you.

trigger: when facing multiple Corpse Slugs and one is low enough to kill this turn
lesson: Killing a Corpse Slug triggers Ravenous, stunning the other slug and preventing its attack. Prioritize lethal on the lowest HP slug to neutralize both threats.
recommendation: If you can kill one Corpse Slug this turn, do so even if it means overkilling slightly, as the stun on the other slug prevents all incoming damage.
anti_pattern: Spreading damage evenly across both slugs instead of focusing one down, which leaves both alive to attack.
counterfactual: Not applicable if neither slug can be killed this turn, or if you have enough block to survive the incoming attacks.

trigger: when you have a multi-hit card (e.g., Sword Boomerang) and need to set up a kill on a Corpse Slug next turn
lesson: Use multi-hit cards early to chip both slugs evenly, then focus fire the lower HP one next turn to trigger Ravenous stun.
recommendation: Play Sword Boomerang or similar multi-hit card first to spread damage, then use single-target attacks to finish the weaker slug.
anti_pattern: Using all single-target attacks on one slug early, leaving the other untouched and both alive to attack.
counterfactual: Not useful if you have enough damage to kill one slug immediately without multi-hit setup.

trigger: when enemy is stunned and you have no lethal damage in hand
lesson: During a stun turn, prioritize setting up future turns (e.g., playing Shrug It Off to draw) over dealing non-lethal damage, as the stun provides a safe turn to improve hand quality.
recommendation: On a stun turn when you cannot kill, play draw or setup cards first before dealing damage, to maximize the chance of drawing into a lethal or defensive line next turn.
anti_pattern: Playing a high-damage attack first on a stun turn when you cannot kill, then using remaining energy on draw, which wastes the stun's safety for hand improvement.
counterfactual: If you have lethal damage in hand, kill immediately regardless of stun.

trigger: when facing two Toadpoles with high HP and one is attacking this turn
lesson: With high HP and Burning Blood, it is often correct to take the 7 damage from an attacking Toadpole to apply Vulnerable with Bash on it, rather than blocking fully. This accelerates the kill and reduces future damage.
recommendation: If you have Bash and the attacking Toadpole is not Vulnerable, consider playing Bash even if you cannot block all incoming damage, provided your HP is high enough to absorb the hit.
anti_pattern: Blocking fully with Defends instead of applying Vulnerable, which delays the kill and may lead to more damage over multiple turns.
counterfactual: Do not apply if your HP is low (below 50%) or if the Toadpole is already Vulnerable.

trigger: when facing two Toadpoles and one is about to apply a Vulnerable buff on its next turn
lesson: Prioritize killing the Toadpole that applies Vulnerable (the buffing one) first, even if the other is attacking. Removing the Vulnerable source reduces future damage and prevents the other Toadpole from dealing increased damage.
recommendation: Focus damage on the buffing Toadpole to eliminate it before it can apply Vulnerable, especially if you have enough damage to kill it in one or two turns.
anti_pattern: Splitting damage evenly between both Toadpoles, allowing the buffing one to survive and apply Vulnerable, which increases incoming damage.
counterfactual: If the attacking Toadpole is about to deal lethal damage this turn, block first instead.

trigger: when enemy has thorns and you have low energy (1-2) and cannot kill this turn
lesson: Against thorns enemies, when you cannot kill this turn, blocking is often better than attacking because the thorns damage plus incoming attack damage exceeds the damage you deal.
recommendation: Calculate net HP loss: if attack damage - thorns damage + incoming enemy damage > block amount, prefer blocking to preserve HP.
anti_pattern: Attacking through thorns when you cannot kill, taking unnecessary thorns damage on top of incoming attack damage.
counterfactual: If you can kill the enemy this turn, attack regardless of thorns.

trigger: when enemy is not attacking this turn and you have lethal damage in hand
lesson: When the enemy is not attacking and you have lethal damage, always kill immediately rather than delaying, even if it costs thorns damage.
recommendation: Prioritize ending the fight on non-attack turns to avoid future damage and statuses.
anti_pattern: Holding attacks or playing blocks when you can kill on a non-attack turn.
counterfactual: If you cannot kill this turn, consider blocking or setting up for next turn.

trigger: when facing multiple Corpse Slugs and one can be killed this turn
lesson: Prioritize killing one Corpse Slug to trigger Ravenous stun on the other, preventing all incoming damage for the turn.
recommendation: Focus all attacks on one Corpse Slug to kill it, even if it means overkilling slightly. The stun from Ravenous is more valuable than splitting damage.
anti_pattern: Splitting damage evenly between two Corpse Slugs instead of focusing one down to trigger the stun.
counterfactual: Not applicable if you cannot kill any Corpse Slug this turn, or if the surviving Slug's attack is negligible.

trigger: when holding Armaments and cannot kill any enemy this turn
lesson: Play Armaments early in a turn when you cannot kill, even if it means taking some damage, to upgrade your hand for future turns.
recommendation: If you have Armaments and cannot secure a kill, play it early to upgrade your hand. The long-term value of upgraded cards outweighs the short-term HP loss from not fully blocking.
anti_pattern: Holding Armaments for a 'better' turn while taking full damage, or playing it late when you could have used the upgraded cards sooner.
counterfactual: Not applicable if you can kill an enemy this turn, or if the incoming damage would be lethal.

trigger: when Corpse Slug is stunned and you have lethal damage next turn
lesson: When Corpse Slug is stunned and you cannot kill it this turn, it is often correct to end turn to save energy and cards for a lethal burst next turn, rather than playing inefficient chip damage.
recommendation: If Corpse Slug is stunned and you lack lethal damage, end turn to preserve energy and draw for a kill next turn.
anti_pattern: Playing Strikes for chip damage when stunned, wasting energy that could secure lethal next turn.
counterfactual: Not applicable if you have enough damage to kill this turn, or if you need to set up block for a non-stun turn.

trigger: when Corpse Slug is at low HP and you have multiple attacks in hand
lesson: Against Corpse Slug, when you have lethal damage in hand, play attacks in any order to trigger Ravenous stun and avoid all damage that turn.
recommendation: If you have enough damage to kill Corpse Slug this turn, play all attacks to trigger Ravenous stun and prevent incoming damage.
anti_pattern: Playing block or non-damage cards when you have lethal damage, wasting the stun opportunity.
counterfactual: Not applicable if you cannot kill this turn, or if the enemy is not Corpse Slug.

trigger: when facing a single enemy that deals moderate attack damage and you have Flame Barrier in hand with enough energy
lesson: Playing Flame Barrier early against a predictable attacker is efficient: it provides sufficient block and returns damage, allowing you to use remaining energy on attacks without needing extra block.
recommendation: If the enemy's attack is fully blocked by Flame Barrier and you have leftover energy, play attacks (e.g., Strike) rather than ending turn, to maximize damage output.
anti_pattern: Do not over-block by playing additional block cards after Flame Barrier if the enemy's attack is already covered.
counterfactual: Not applicable if the enemy's attack is multi-hit or ignores block, or if you have low HP and need to preserve block for future turns.

trigger: when you have Bash and a high-damage attack (e.g., Headbutt) in hand with enough energy to play both, and the enemy is not about to attack for lethal
lesson: Sequencing Bash before a high-damage attack like Headbutt maximizes total damage due to Vulnerable, and can set up lethal in the following turn.
recommendation: Play Bash first to apply Vulnerable, then follow with your strongest attack to capitalize on the 50% damage boost. Plan the remaining damage needed for lethal next turn.
anti_pattern: Do not play a high-damage attack before Bash if you have enough energy to play both, as you lose the Vulnerable multiplier.
counterfactual: Not applicable if the enemy has artifact or is immune to Vulnerable, or if you need to save energy for block.

trigger: when enemy has lethal HP and Bash is in hand with 2 energy available
lesson: Bash's 8 damage is often enough to finish low-HP Sludge Spinner, ending combat before its high-damage attack.
recommendation: Prioritize lethal with Bash over other plays when Sludge Spinner is at ≤8 HP and you have 2 energy.
anti_pattern: Holding Bash for Vulnerable application when lethal is available, prolonging combat and taking unnecessary damage.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy has block or intangible, or if Bash is needed for a higher-priority target.

trigger: when facing multiple low-HP enemies and holding an AoE attack that can kill or cripple most of them
lesson: Sacrificing a moderate amount of HP (e.g., 14) to play a high-damage AoE card early is often correct when it eliminates or severely weakens multiple enemies, reducing incoming damage over the fight.
recommendation: Evaluate the trade-off: if the AoE damage can kill at least one enemy and leave others near death, the HP loss is acceptable, especially with post-combat healing like Burning Blood.
anti_pattern: Avoid hoarding AoE cards for later turns when immediate use can prevent multiple enemy attacks.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the AoE damage is insufficient to kill or significantly reduce any enemy, or if the HP loss would put you in lethal range of the next attack.

trigger: when facing Sewer Clam with Plating and have a multi-hit or high-damage card
lesson: Against Sewer Clam, prioritize breaking its Plating each turn before dealing HP damage, as Plating resets to 7-8 block at turn start.
recommendation: Use a single high-damage attack or multi-hit card first to strip Plating, then follow up with other attacks to maximize HP damage.
anti_pattern: Playing multiple small attacks without breaking Plating first, wasting damage on block.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy has no Plating or if you can one-shot through block.

trigger: when holding Armaments and have at least 1 energy and hand size >= 3
lesson: Armaments is a high-value early turn play: it upgrades all cards in hand for the rest of combat, providing long-term scaling, and gives block.
recommendation: Play Armaments as the first action of the turn if you have energy and a hand with multiple useful cards to upgrade.
anti_pattern: Delaying Armaments to later turns when you could have upgraded more cards earlier.
counterfactual: Skip if you need immediate damage to survive lethal or if hand has no impactful upgrades.

trigger: enemy has buff intent and has block
lesson: When enemy is buffing and has block, it is often correct to skip attacking if your attacks would only strip block without dealing HP damage, saving energy and cards for the next turn.
recommendation: If enemy intent is buff and they have block, evaluate whether your attacks can deal meaningful HP damage after breaking block. If not, end turn to preserve resources.
anti_pattern: Wasting energy and attack cards to remove block when enemy is not attacking, leaving you with fewer options on the next turn.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you have enough damage to break block and deal significant HP damage, or if the enemy's buff is dangerous and must be prevented.

trigger: when at high HP (>75%) and enemy is not lethal this turn
lesson: Taking moderate damage (e.g., 14-18) while at high HP is acceptable to preserve potions for harder fights later in the act.
recommendation: When HP is above 75% and the enemy is not threatening lethal, prefer to take damage rather than use potions or block inefficiently. Potions are scarce resources best saved for elite or boss fights.
anti_pattern: Using potions or playing inefficient block cards when at high HP, wasting resources that could be critical later.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the damage would put you below 50% HP, or if the enemy has scaling damage that could become lethal in subsequent turns.

trigger: when facing multiple Corpse Slugs and you have a kill line on one enemy this turn
lesson: Killing a Corpse Slug stuns all remaining Corpse Slugs for the turn, preventing all incoming damage. Prioritize sequencing attacks to kill one enemy rather than spreading damage.
recommendation: When you can kill a Corpse Slug this turn, do so even if it means forgoing block, because the stun from Ravenous will prevent all damage from the other Slugs.
anti_pattern: Playing block cards when you could instead kill a Corpse Slug and stun the rest, wasting damage potential.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you cannot kill any Corpse Slug this turn, or if the stun does not prevent enough damage to justify the risk.
