trigger: when you have Flame Barrier in hand and enemies are attacking for significant damage
lesson: Flame Barrier provides both block and retaliation. Playing it early in a turn against multiple attacking enemies maximizes value by blocking damage and dealing damage back to all attackers.
recommendation: Play Flame Barrier as the first card in a turn when facing multiple attacking enemies, as the retaliation applies to all enemies that attack that turn.
anti_pattern: Playing Flame Barrier late in a turn after other block cards, wasting the block potential and missing retaliation on enemies that already attacked.
counterfactual: Do not apply if enemies are not attacking this turn, or if you have enough block from other sources to fully mitigate damage.

trigger: when both Corpse Slugs are stunned and you have Armaments in hand with 1+ energy
lesson: Use Armaments during a free turn (both enemies stunned) to upgrade your entire hand, as the opportunity cost is zero and the long-term benefit is high.
recommendation: When both Corpse Slugs are stunned and you have Armaments, play it to upgrade all cards in hand before dealing damage or blocking.
anti_pattern: Playing a Strike or other damage card instead of Armaments when both enemies are stunned, wasting the free upgrade opportunity.
counterfactual: Do not apply if Armaments is not in hand or if you have lethal damage this turn.

trigger: when one Corpse Slug is low HP (≤6) and the other is alive, and you have enough damage to kill the low one
lesson: Kill a low-HP Corpse Slug first to trigger Ravenous, stunning the other slug and preventing all incoming damage that turn.
recommendation: Focus damage on the lowest-HP Corpse Slug to trigger its death and stun the other, nullifying their attack for the turn.
anti_pattern: Splitting damage evenly between both slugs, allowing both to attack and take unnecessary damage.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you cannot kill any slug this turn, or if the other slug is already stunned.

trigger: enemy is stunned and you have 1 energy with no lethal
lesson: When enemy is stunned and you cannot kill, playing a Strike for chip damage is correct; ending turn wastes energy and delays kill.
recommendation: Play any available attack for damage even if not lethal; do not end turn with energy when enemy is stunned.
anti_pattern: Ending turn with energy while enemy is stunned and you have attacks in hand.
counterfactual: If you have no attacks or enemy is not stunned, this does not apply.

trigger: enemy HP is low enough that a Strike + Headbutt sequence is lethal
lesson: Against Corpse Slug, sequence attacks to kill in one turn when possible; play lower-damage attack first to avoid overkill waste.
recommendation: When lethal with two attacks, play the weaker attack first to confirm damage, then the stronger attack for the kill.
anti_pattern: Playing the stronger attack first risks overkill if the weaker attack would have been sufficient.
counterfactual: If enemy has block or intangible, adjust order accordingly.

trigger: when enemy is about to attack and you have block cards in hand
lesson: Against Terror Eel, prioritize full blocking its attacks over dealing damage when HP is below 50%. The enemy's damage output is consistent and can quickly snowball if you take chip damage.
recommendation: When facing Terror Eel with less than 50% HP, always ensure you can fully block its attack before dealing damage. Use Shrug It Off and Defend to reach exact block values, even if it means delaying damage.
anti_pattern: Taking chip damage to deal a few points of damage when you could have fully blocked, especially when not close to the 70 HP stun threshold.
counterfactual: If you are above 50% HP or very close to the 70 HP stun threshold (within 10-15 damage), it may be worth taking some damage to push through the stun.

trigger: when enemy is stunned (below 70 HP) and you have Vulnerable applied
lesson: When Terror Eel is stunned, maximize damage output by playing all attacks in hand, even if it means overkilling. The stun turn is a free turn to push through the second half of its HP.
recommendation: On the stun turn, play all attacks from highest to lowest damage to maximize the free damage window. Do not play block cards or cycle cards unless you need to find lethal damage.
anti_pattern: Playing block cards or Shrug It Off for draw during the stun turn when you could be dealing damage, wasting the free turn.
counterfactual: If you have no attacks in hand, use the stun turn to cycle with Shrug It Off or set up with Armaments.

trigger: when low HP (below 25%) and enemy attack is known
lesson: Prioritize full block over damage when HP is critical, even if it means using multiple block cards or delaying damage output.
recommendation: When HP is critically low, calculate exact block needed to survive the turn and play block cards first to ensure survival, then use remaining energy for damage if safe.
anti_pattern: Do not gamble on taking damage to save block cards when HP is critically low; the gold loss penalty for taking damage makes this especially costly.
counterfactual: If HP is high (above 50%) or enemy attack is weak, it may be acceptable to take some damage to save block cards for later.

trigger: when having a draw-positive attack (e.g., Pommel Strike) and block is already sufficient for the turn
lesson: Play draw-positive attacks after securing block to cycle through the deck faster and find key cards for future turns.
recommendation: After establishing sufficient block for the turn, use remaining energy on attacks that draw cards (like Pommel Strike) to improve hand quality for the next turn.
anti_pattern: Do not end turn with unspent energy when you have draw-positive attacks in hand and block is already covered.
counterfactual: If the enemy has a very large attack next turn that requires specific block cards, consider saving energy for defensive options instead.

trigger: when Gremlin Merc is below 17 HP and you have 0 energy with Howl from Beyond in hand
lesson: Howl from Beyond deals 16 damage, which can set up lethal next turn against Gremlin Merc (47 HP) when combined with a 9-damage attack like Headbutt.
recommendation: Play Howl from Beyond when enemy HP is between 17 and 32 to enable a two-turn kill with a 9-damage follow-up, even at 0 energy.
anti_pattern: Holding Howl from Beyond for later when it could immediately reduce lethal threshold.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy has block or you have better damage scaling.

trigger: when both enemies are stunned and you have Armaments in hand with at least 1 energy
lesson: Play Armaments to upgrade all hand cards when no enemy is attacking, even if block is irrelevant, to scale damage for future turns.
recommendation: Use Armaments early in a safe turn to upgrade Strikes and Defends, increasing damage output and block efficiency for the rest of the combat.
anti_pattern: Holding Armaments for a later turn when you could upgrade more cards now, or playing a block card when no attack is incoming.
counterfactual: Do not play Armaments if you need immediate damage to kill an enemy this turn to avoid lethal damage next turn.

trigger: when you have a high-damage attack (e.g., Howl from Beyond) and can kill one enemy while heavily damaging another, even if you take some damage in return
lesson: Prioritize killing a high-value enemy (e.g., Fat Gremlin for gold) with a powerful attack, accepting moderate damage, to secure rewards and simplify the fight.
recommendation: Use a strong attack to eliminate a priority target (e.g., Fat Gremlin) even if it leaves you vulnerable, as the long-term benefit (gold, reduced incoming damage) outweighs the temporary HP loss.
anti_pattern: Playing multiple small attacks inefficiently or holding a powerful attack for a later turn when you could secure a kill now.
counterfactual: Do not take lethal damage or leave yourself unable to block a fatal attack next turn.

trigger: when facing Living Fog with a hand containing Shrug It Off and sufficient block to survive the turn
lesson: Playing Shrug It Off for block even when already safe is valuable for deck cycling and finding key cards like Inflame or Armaments earlier.
recommendation: When you have excess block capacity and Shrug It Off in hand, play it for the draw even if block is already sufficient, to dig for scaling or setup cards.
anti_pattern: Holding Shrug It Off for later when current block is already sufficient, missing the opportunity to cycle the deck.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the draw could cause a status card to be drawn that would dilute a critical hand next turn.

trigger: when facing Living Fog with Inflame and Armaments in hand on turn 2
lesson: Playing Inflame before Armaments on the same turn maximizes the value of Armaments' upgrade by ensuring the upgraded cards benefit from the Strength gain immediately.
recommendation: Sequence Inflame before Armaments so that the upgraded attacks in hand deal increased damage from the Strength buff on the same turn.
anti_pattern: Playing Armaments before Inflame, which would upgrade cards without the Strength bonus applying to attacks played that turn.
counterfactual: Do not apply if Armaments is needed for block to survive the turn and Inflame would waste energy that could be used for block.

trigger: Gas Bomb is alive and has lethal DeathBlow next turn
lesson: Prioritize killing Gas Bomb this turn even if it means using a low-cost attack that draws cards, because the DeathBlow threat outweighs the value of saving energy or cards for other enemies.
recommendation: When Gas Bomb is at low HP and will use DeathBlow next turn, use the cheapest attack that can finish it, especially if it also draws cards to improve your hand for the remaining enemy.
anti_pattern: Holding back a cheap attack to save energy or cards for a different enemy when Gas Bomb can kill you next turn.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you have enough block or intangible to survive the DeathBlow, or if Gas Bomb is not using DeathBlow next turn.

trigger: when facing Living Fog at low HP and enemy has not yet summoned a minion
lesson: Flame Barrier is a high-value defensive play against Living Fog when at critical HP, as it blocks all incoming damage and deals retaliatory damage without requiring additional energy next turn.
recommendation: When at very low HP against Living Fog and you have Flame Barrier in hand, play it even if it exhausts all energy, as it prevents lethal damage and sets up a safe transition to the next turn.
anti_pattern: Do not gamble on offensive plays when at critical HP against Living Fog, as its attack can kill you before you get another turn.
counterfactual: If you have sufficient HP to survive the incoming attack, a more aggressive line may be better to race the summon.

trigger: when you have Shuriken and are in a multi-attack turn against Living Fog before it summons
lesson: Against Living Fog, sequencing Headbutt before Strikes maximizes Shuriken value by ensuring the 3-attack threshold is met, granting +1 Strength for subsequent turns.
recommendation: Play Headbutt first (counts as 1 attack), then follow with two Strikes to trigger Shuriken, gaining Strength for future turns while dealing consistent damage.
anti_pattern: Do not play Strikes before Headbutt, as this may waste the Shuriken trigger if you run out of energy or attacks.
counterfactual: If you lack Shuriken or have a different attack density, this specific sequencing is less critical.

trigger: when facing multiple enemies and one enemy deals lethal damage this turn
lesson: Prioritize eliminating the highest-threat enemy first, even if it costs more energy, to reduce incoming damage below lethal threshold.
recommendation: Calculate lethal damage from each enemy and use high-damage attacks (e.g., Bash) to remove the most dangerous target, then block remaining damage.
anti_pattern: Spreading damage across enemies or blocking first when one enemy's attack alone is lethal.
counterfactual: Not applicable if both enemies' attacks are survivable or if you can block all damage.

trigger: when Living Fog has applied Smoggy (skills unplayable) and you have block cards in hand
lesson: When Smoggy prevents skill play, prioritize playing block cards before attacks to ensure survival against the incoming attack, then use remaining energy on attacks.
recommendation: Play Defend first to establish block, then use remaining energy on attacks like Strike and Iron Wave to maximize damage while staying safe.
anti_pattern: Playing attacks first when Smoggy is active, leaving insufficient energy for block and risking lethal damage.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy is not attacking this turn or if you have enough block from other sources.

trigger: when Living Fog is below 20 HP and you have 3 energy with attack cards available
lesson: Against low-HP Living Fog, sequence Iron Wave before Strike to gain block while dealing damage, ensuring full survival against the next attack.
recommendation: Play Iron Wave first for block + damage, then Strike for pure damage, ending with enough block to survive the enemy's turn.
anti_pattern: Playing Strike first and leaving insufficient energy for Iron Wave's block, risking unnecessary damage.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy is not attacking or if you have other block sources.

trigger: when facing Gas Bomb and Living Fog with low HP and enough energy to kill Gas Bomb with a Strike
lesson: Killing Gas Bomb first with a cheap attack is a high-value sequencing priority because it removes the most dangerous damage source early.
recommendation: Use a low-cost attack (e.g., Strike) to eliminate Gas Bomb on the same turn if possible, then allocate remaining energy to block or damage the remaining enemy.
anti_pattern: Do not waste high-cost attacks on Gas Bomb when a Strike suffices, as that wastes energy needed for defense or finishing Living Fog.
counterfactual: If Gas Bomb is not lethal with a cheap attack, consider blocking first or using a multi-hit attack to break its block.

trigger: when enemy is at very low HP (≤2) and you have a Strike or any 1-cost attack in hand with 1 energy remaining
lesson: When enemy is at 2 HP and you have 1 energy, a basic Strike is sufficient for lethal. Do not overcomplicate by playing a higher-damage card or a block card first.
recommendation: Play the cheapest attack that deals at least the remaining enemy HP to secure lethal, preserving other resources.
anti_pattern: Playing a block card or a more expensive attack when a basic Strike already kills wastes energy and card advantage.
counterfactual: If the enemy has Intangible or block, this does not apply.

trigger: when enemy is about to attack and you have Flame Barrier in hand with 2+ energy
lesson: Flame Barrier is a high-value block card that also provides thorns; prioritize it over other block options when facing a boss that attacks frequently.
recommendation: Play Flame Barrier early in the turn to maximize block and set up thorns for future attacks, even if it leaves 1 energy unused.
anti_pattern: Playing a lower-block card like Armaments (5 block) instead of Flame Barrier (12 block) when you have 3 energy and no other high-impact play.
counterfactual: If the enemy is not attacking this turn or has a multi-hit attack that would make thorns less effective, consider other options.

trigger: when you have Inflame in hand and enough energy to play it plus at least one other card
lesson: Play Inflame early in the turn to boost all subsequent attacks, especially when you have multiple attacks in hand.
recommendation: Play Inflame first before any attacks to maximize the strength gain across all attacks played that turn.
anti_pattern: Playing attacks first and then Inflame, missing the strength bonus on those attacks.
counterfactual: If you need immediate block to survive and Inflame doesn't provide block, delay it until a safer turn.

trigger: when Soul Fysh has Intangible and you have a Flex Potion and Bash in hand
lesson: Against Soul Fysh with Intangible, use Flex Potion before Bash to maximize damage per hit through the damage cap, and apply Vulnerable for subsequent turns.
recommendation: Play Flex Potion first, then Bash to apply Vulnerable, then follow with highest-damage attacks. This sequences damage efficiently through Intangible's per-hit cap.
anti_pattern: Playing Bash before Flex Potion wastes the strength bonus on a single hit that's already capped by Intangible.
counterfactual: Not applicable if Soul Fysh does not have Intangible, or if you lack Flex Potion.

trigger: when Soul Fysh has Intangible and you have Armaments in hand with energy for other cards
lesson: Against Soul Fysh with Intangible, play Armaments early in the turn to upgrade hand cards, since the damage cap makes each hit less impactful and upgrading provides long-term value.
recommendation: Play Armaments before other attacks to upgrade your hand, then use remaining energy on attacks or block. The upgrade benefit outweighs delaying a single capped-damage attack.
anti_pattern: Playing attacks first and Armaments last wastes the upgrade opportunity on cards that could have been stronger for future turns.
counterfactual: Not applicable if Soul Fysh does not have Intangible, or if you need immediate damage to finish the fight.

trigger: when Beckon status cards are in hand and enemy is not attacking or block is insufficient
lesson: Beckon status cards deal 6 HP loss at end of turn if not played. Prioritize playing Beckon over inefficient attacks or blocks when it prevents self-damage, even if it wastes energy.
recommendation: When holding a Beckon and you have spare energy, play it to avoid the 6 HP loss. Only skip playing it if you can fully block the enemy attack AND the Beckon damage, or if the turn is lethal anyway.
anti_pattern: Ending turn with Beckon in hand when you have unspent energy and no critical need to save that energy for next turn.
counterfactual: Do not play Beckon if you need the energy for a critical block or damage card that prevents death this turn, or if you have enough block to absorb both the attack and the Beckon damage.

trigger: when HP is below 25% and enemy is about to attack for lethal damage
lesson: Against Soul Fysh, once HP drops below the threshold where you cannot survive the next attack plus any Beckon damage, the fight is effectively lost. Prioritize aggressive damage output in earlier turns to avoid reaching this state.
recommendation: When HP is low (below ~25%), calculate whether you can survive the next enemy attack plus any Beckon self-damage. If not, the only viable play is to maximize damage output in hopes of killing the enemy before it attacks. Do not waste energy on block that won't save you.
anti_pattern: Playing defensive cards (block, Shrug It Off) when the incoming damage exceeds your max HP, instead of maximizing damage to end the fight.
counterfactual: This applies only when death is guaranteed regardless of block. If you can survive with block, still prioritize blocking.

trigger: when facing Nibbit with high HP and a hand of Strikes and Bash
lesson: Against Nibbit, aggressive damage racing is optimal when HP is high; its damage output is low enough that blocking is unnecessary.
recommendation: Play all Strikes and Bash each turn to maximize damage, accepting Nibbit's attacks. Only block if HP drops below 50%.
anti_pattern: Playing Defend cards against Nibbit when HP is high, which delays the kill and wastes energy.
counterfactual: Not applicable when facing enemies with higher damage output or when HP is low.

trigger: when starting turn 2 against Nibbit with Bash and Strikes in hand
lesson: Play Bash first to apply Vulnerable, then follow with Strikes to maximize damage output for the turn.
recommendation: Always play Bash before Strikes when both are available, as the Vulnerable debuff increases subsequent Strike damage by 50%.
anti_pattern: Playing Strikes before Bash, missing the damage multiplier from Vulnerable.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy is immune to Vulnerable or if Bash would overkill.

trigger: when enemy is not attacking and hand has Burning Pact with 3+ energy
lesson: Burning Pact is a strong early-game play on non-attack turns to cycle into damage or scaling while thinning the deck.
recommendation: Play Burning Pact early when safe to do so, especially with 3 energy, to dig for key cards and exhaust a basic Strike.
anti_pattern: Holding Burning Pact for too long or playing it on a turn when blocking is needed.
counterfactual: Do not play if hand already has critical damage/block and energy is needed for other plays.

trigger: enemy has non-attack intent and you have high HP (>75%)
lesson: When enemy has non-attack intent and HP is high, prioritize spending all energy on damage over blocking or saving energy.
recommendation: Play all damage cards in hand when enemy is not attacking and you have ample HP. Do not hold energy or play blocks.
anti_pattern: Playing Defend or ending turn with unspent energy when enemy is not attacking and HP is high.
counterfactual: Do not apply if enemy has attack intent or if HP is low enough that future damage is lethal.

trigger: you have Bash in hand with 3 energy and enemy has non-attack intent
lesson: With Bash and 3 energy against a non-attacking enemy, play Bash first to apply Vulnerable, then follow with Strikes to maximize damage output over the next two turns.
recommendation: Sequence: Bash (2 energy) -> Strike (1 energy). This applies Vulnerable for 2 turns, increasing subsequent Strike damage by 50%.
anti_pattern: Playing Strikes before Bash, which misses the Vulnerable damage bonus.
counterfactual: Do not apply if enemy will attack next turn and you need to block, or if you have no Strikes to follow up.

trigger: when facing multiple slimes including a Twig Slime (S) that is attacking this turn
lesson: Bash on the attacking Twig Slime (S) is a high-value play because it removes the only damage source this turn and applies Vulnerable to the next enemy.
recommendation: Prioritize killing the attacking Twig Slime (S) with Bash over other targets, even if it costs 2 energy, as it neutralizes immediate threat and sets up future damage.
anti_pattern: Do not waste Bash on a non-attacking slime or a slime that is not the primary damage source this turn.
counterfactual: If the Twig Slime (S) is not attacking this turn (e.g., stunned or buffing), consider other targets or saving energy.

trigger: when hand contains Burning Pact and a low-value card (e.g., Defend) and no incoming damage this turn
lesson: Burning Pact can be used to cycle through starter cards for free when you have spare energy and no immediate threat.
recommendation: Play Burning Pact targeting a Defend or Strike when you have 1+ energy and no incoming damage to improve next turn's hand.
anti_pattern: Holding Burning Pact for later when you could use it now to thin the deck and draw into better cards.
counterfactual: Do not play if you need the energy for a critical block or damage this turn, or if the card to exhaust is a key scaling card.

trigger: when facing multiple slimes and the small slime is about to attack for non-trivial damage
lesson: Prioritize eliminating the small slime first to reduce incoming damage, even if it costs a high-damage card like Unrelenting.
recommendation: Use a high-damage attack to kill the small slime early, then follow up with free attacks on the medium slime to maximize damage output while minimizing future damage taken.
anti_pattern: Saving high-damage cards for the medium slime while letting the small slime attack multiple times.
counterfactual: If the small slime is not attacking or its damage is negligible, consider other sequencing.

trigger: when enemy is at low HP (≤9) and will not attack next turn, and you have Unrelenting in hand
lesson: With Unrelenting, sequence attacks to maximize damage in a single turn even without lethal: play Unrelenting first (12 damage, makes next attack free), then Bash (8 damage free) to leave enemy at 1 HP with Vulnerable applied, ensuring easy kill next turn.
recommendation: When enemy HP is low and no lethal this turn, use Unrelenting to make a high-damage attack free, then play Bash (or another attack) for free to maximize damage and apply Vulnerable for next turn.
anti_pattern: Don't play Bash first (costs 2 energy) then Unrelenting (costs 2 energy) - you'd run out of energy and miss the free attack synergy.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy will attack next turn and you need to block, or if you have lethal without Unrelenting.

trigger: when you have high HP (>50) and enemy attack is small (≤8) on first turn
lesson: With high HP and a weak enemy attack, it's optimal to play all attacks (even taking damage) rather than blocking, to accelerate the kill and minimize future damage.
recommendation: On turn 1 with high HP and small enemy attack, play all Strikes/attacks for damage instead of blocking - the HP loss is acceptable and speeds up the fight.
anti_pattern: Don't waste energy on block cards when you have high HP and enemy damage is low - this delays the kill and may cause more damage over time.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy has a strong upcoming attack pattern or if you have low HP.

trigger: when facing two enemies where one scales (Snapping Jaxfruit) and the other is a support (Flyconid)
lesson: Prioritize damaging the scaling enemy (Snapping Jaxfruit) early, even if it means taking more damage from the support, to prevent its strength gain from snowballing.
recommendation: Focus attacks on the scaling enemy first, using multi-hit or free-attack cards (e.g., Unrelenting) to maximize damage per turn, and only block if lethal damage is imminent.
anti_pattern: Splitting damage evenly between both enemies, allowing the scaling enemy to survive and grow stronger.
counterfactual: If the support enemy deals lethal damage or applies a debilitating debuff, consider blocking or killing it first.

trigger: when having 0 energy and no playable cards in hand, but a potion is available
lesson: Using a potion (e.g., Colorless Potion) when out of energy and no playable cards can generate a free card that may kill a low-HP enemy or provide block, outweighing the risk of wasting the potion.
recommendation: If the potion is free to use and could potentially generate a useful card (attack or block), use it instead of ending turn, especially if an enemy is near death.
anti_pattern: Hoarding potions for later and ending turn without using them when they could have prevented damage or secured a kill.
counterfactual: If the potion has a cost (e.g., energy) or is a rare potion better saved for a boss, consider saving it.

trigger: when facing a multi-enemy encounter with one low-HP threat and Dramatic Entrance is in hand
lesson: Dramatic Entrance can instantly remove a low-HP enemy and damage the other, effectively reducing incoming damage for zero energy cost.
recommendation: Play Dramatic Entrance early if it can eliminate a threatening enemy or significantly reduce the number of attackers, even if it means taking some unblocked damage.
anti_pattern: Holding Dramatic Entrance for a 'better' multi-target moment when immediate removal of a threat is available.
counterfactual: Do not play if the damage is insufficient to kill any enemy or if the remaining enemy's attack would be lethal.

trigger: when facing Flyconid with lethal damage available this turn and Inflame in hand
lesson: Play Inflame before Strikes to maximize damage output and secure lethal, avoiding Flyconid's attack and Frail debuff.
recommendation: If you have Inflame and enough Strikes to kill Flyconid this turn, play Inflame first to boost damage, then Strikes.
anti_pattern: Playing Strikes before Inflame or holding Inflame for later when lethal is possible this turn.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you cannot kill Flyconid this turn or if you need to block instead.

trigger: when enemy is not attacking this turn and you have a power card in hand
lesson: Play scaling powers like Inflame on safe turns when the enemy is not attacking, to maximize long-term damage output without sacrificing block.
recommendation: Prioritize playing Inflame (or similar scaling powers) on turns with no incoming damage to set up strength for the rest of the fight.
anti_pattern: Holding a power card for later when a safe turn is available, wasting the opportunity to scale early.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the enemy is attacking this turn and you lack sufficient block to survive.

trigger: when you have Unrelenting and a 0-cost attack (e.g., Breakthrough) in hand on a safe turn
lesson: Sequence Unrelenting before a 0-cost attack to maximize damage: Unrelenting makes the next attack free, allowing you to play a high-damage 0-cost card without spending energy.
recommendation: Play Unrelenting first, then follow with a 0-cost attack like Breakthrough to get efficient damage output on safe turns.
anti_pattern: Playing the 0-cost attack before Unrelenting, missing the free attack synergy.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the enemy is attacking and you need to block instead.

trigger: when enemy is not attacking this turn and you have lethal damage in hand
lesson: Against Phrog Parasite, when it is not attacking, it is safe to spend all energy on attacks to kill it this turn, avoiding its status card attack next turn.
recommendation: Calculate if you can kill this turn. If yes, play all attacks. If no, consider playing Bloodletting first to gain extra energy for more attacks.
anti_pattern: Playing defensively (block) when enemy is not attacking and you have lethal damage, prolonging the fight and taking unnecessary damage.
counterfactual: Do not apply if enemy is attacking this turn and you cannot kill it; then you must block.

trigger: when you have Bloodletting in hand and need more energy to play multiple attacks this turn
lesson: Play Bloodletting before other attacks to gain energy without spending current energy, enabling more attacks in the same turn.
recommendation: Always play Bloodletting first if you plan to play multiple attacks, as it gives net +2 energy and the HP cost is negligible.
anti_pattern: Playing attacks first and then Bloodletting, wasting the energy gain.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you are at very low HP (e.g., below 10) and the 3 HP cost could kill you.

trigger: when all enemies are stunned and you have no immediate threat
lesson: Ending turn when all enemies are stunned is optimal to cycle cards and preserve block cards for when they are needed.
recommendation: If all enemies are stunned and you have no need for block this turn, end turn to draw fresh cards rather than playing block cards that will be wasted.
anti_pattern: Playing block cards like Defend when enemies are stunned, wasting block that could be used on a future turn.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you have a critical power or setup card that must be played now regardless of enemy state.

trigger: when you have Burning Pact and Feel No Pain in hand against multiple Wrigglers
lesson: Burning Pact can exhaust an unplayable Infection card to trigger Feel No Pain block and draw more cards, creating a strong defensive turn.
recommendation: Play Burning Pact targeting an Infection or other unplayable status card first to gain block from Feel No Pain and draw into more options before playing other cards.
anti_pattern: Playing Burning Pact on a playable card when you have Infections in hand, missing the opportunity to exhaust a dead card.
counterfactual: Do not apply if you have no Feel No Pain in play or if the drawn cards are unlikely to improve your position.

trigger: when facing multiple Wrigglers and one is at very low HP
lesson: Prioritize killing a low-HP Wriggler even if it costs a free attack, because Wrigglers scale HP when others die, so delaying the kill can make it harder to finish later.
recommendation: When a Wriggler is at 3 HP or less and you have a free attack, kill it immediately rather than saving the attack for a different target.
anti_pattern: Hesitating to kill a low-HP Wriggler because you want to save the attack for a different enemy, allowing it to scale up.
counterfactual: Not applicable if the Wriggler is not at lethal range or if you lack the damage to kill it this turn.

trigger: when at very low HP (below 5) and facing lethal damage next turn
lesson: Bloodletting can be a desperation play to gain energy for a game-winning sequence, even when it costs HP, if ending turn means certain death.
recommendation: When HP is critically low and you will die if you end turn, consider using Bloodletting to gain energy for a lethal or blocking sequence, even if it costs 3 HP.
anti_pattern: Hoarding Bloodletting for later when immediate death is guaranteed without its energy.
counterfactual: Not applicable if you have enough block or damage to survive without the extra energy, or if Bloodletting would kill you outright.

trigger: when facing multiple Wrigglers and one is about to attack while the other is buffing
lesson: Prioritize killing the attacking Wriggler over damaging the buffing one, even if the buffing one has lower HP, because removing the immediate attack threat prevents lethal damage.
recommendation: Focus damage on the Wriggler that is attacking this turn, especially if you lack block. The buffing Wriggler can be dealt with next turn.
anti_pattern: Splitting damage evenly or focusing the buffing Wriggler first, which leaves the attacking threat alive.
counterfactual: If you have enough block to survive the attack, or if the buffing Wriggler's buff is game-ending (e.g., strength scaling), then reconsider.

trigger: when at critically low HP (≤ 25%) and enemy is within lethal range of a single attack
lesson: Prioritize lethal damage over blocking or setup when at 1 HP, even if the enemy is not attacking this turn, to avoid any risk of future damage.
recommendation: If you have a card that can deal lethal damage to the enemy, play it immediately regardless of the enemy's current intent, as any delay risks death from an unexpected attack or status effect.
anti_pattern: Ending turn or playing defensive cards when at 1 HP and lethal damage is available, assuming safety because the enemy is not attacking this turn.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the enemy has intangible or block that would prevent lethal damage this turn.

trigger: when facing multiple Inklets with low HP and need to break Slippery
lesson: Against multiple Inklets, prioritize breaking Slippery on one target with a cheap attack (e.g., Pillage) before committing high-damage attacks, to ensure damage lands and set up a kill.
recommendation: Use a 0- or 1-cost attack to break Slippery on the target you plan to kill, then follow up with Bash or Strike to maximize damage efficiency.
anti_pattern: Playing high-cost attacks first without breaking Slippery, wasting damage if the enemy becomes intangible.
counterfactual: Not applicable if you have enough damage to kill through Slippery or if the enemy is already vulnerable.

trigger: when HP is between 25-50% and considering Bloodletting
lesson: Bloodletting's 3 HP loss is acceptable when HP is not critical (above 25%) and the energy gain enables killing an enemy this turn, reducing incoming damage.
recommendation: Play Bloodletting to gain energy for lethal or near-lethal damage, even at low HP, if it prevents taking more damage next turn.
anti_pattern: Hoarding energy or playing defensively when Bloodletting could enable a kill that saves more HP than it costs.
counterfactual: Do not play Bloodletting if HP is below 25% or if the energy cannot be used to significantly reduce enemy count or damage output.

trigger: when facing multiple Inklets with Slippery and have a card that breaks Slippery (e.g., Unrelenting) and a 0-cost attack in hand
lesson: Use a low-damage Slippery-breaking card first to enable free attacks, then prioritize using free attacks to damage one Inklet before spending energy on block.
recommendation: Play Unrelenting on one Inklet to break Slippery and make next attack free, then use the free Strike on the same target to maximize damage per energy.
anti_pattern: Using a high-damage card first against Slippery wastes damage; avoid playing Strike before breaking Slippery.
counterfactual: If you have no free attack or the Slippery-breaking card costs too much energy, this sequence may not be optimal.

trigger: when HP is low (below 30) and facing lethal or near-lethal damage from multiple Inklets
lesson: Using a healing potion early to survive a big hit can be better than saving it, especially if it enables you to kill an enemy that turn.
recommendation: If you can kill or significantly damage an enemy after healing, use the potion immediately to avoid death and preserve HP for later turns.
anti_pattern: Saving a healing potion when you would die or take heavy damage without it; hoarding potions can lead to unnecessary HP loss.
counterfactual: If you have enough block to survive without healing, or if the potion is more valuable later (e.g., against a boss), consider saving it.

trigger: when enemy is at very low HP (≤3) and you have lethal with a basic Strike
lesson: Prefer the cheapest lethal over overkill or setup cards to avoid unnecessary damage intake.
recommendation: Use the lowest-cost card that secures lethal, even if it leaves energy unused. Do not play expensive attacks or buffs when a Strike finishes the fight.
anti_pattern: Playing a higher-cost attack (e.g., Bash) or a setup card (e.g., Inflame) when a Strike already kills, risking extra damage from enemy attack.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy has a multi-hit attack that could kill you next turn and you have block cards; then consider blocking first.

trigger: when facing Twig Slime (M) with a free-attack enabler (e.g., Unrelenting) and AoE damage available
lesson: Prioritize AoE (Breakthrough) first to chip both enemies, then use Unrelenting on Twig Slime to set up a free Strike, finishing it efficiently. This sequence maximizes damage output and reduces incoming status cards.
recommendation: Play AoE card first, then Unrelenting on Twig Slime, then free Strike to kill or nearly kill it.
anti_pattern: Do not play Unrelenting before AoE, as it wastes the free-attack potential on a lower-value target.
counterfactual: If Twig Slime is already low HP or you lack AoE, adjust sequence to focus single-target damage.

trigger: when Twig Slime (M) is at 1 HP and you have a Strike or any 1-damage attack
lesson: Killing Twig Slime (M) as soon as possible is critical to stop its Constrict status and reduce incoming damage. Even if you take some damage this turn, the long-term benefit outweighs the short-term HP loss.
recommendation: Use any available attack to finish off Twig Slime (M) when it is at 1 HP, even if it means taking damage from the other enemy.
anti_pattern: Do not delay killing Twig Slime (M) to play a power like Feel No Pain first, as the status cards will accumulate.
counterfactual: If you are at very low HP and would die to the other enemy's attack, consider blocking first.

trigger: when you have high HP (>75%) and Inflame in hand on turn 1 against a moderate-attacking enemy
lesson: Playing Inflame early when HP is high is safe and accelerates damage output, shortening the fight.
recommendation: Prioritize Inflame on turn 1 if HP is high and enemy attack is moderate; the strength gain outweighs the damage taken.
anti_pattern: Delaying Inflame to block first when HP is high, which prolongs the fight and wastes scaling potential.
counterfactual: Do not apply if HP is low (<50%) or enemy has a very high damage attack that could lead to lethal.

trigger: when you have Bloodletting, Bash, and enough damage to kill the enemy this turn
lesson: Use Bloodletting to gain energy for a lethal burst sequence: Bash (Vulnerable) then attacks.
recommendation: Sequence Bloodletting first for energy, then Bash to apply Vulnerable, then follow with high-damage attacks to secure lethal.
anti_pattern: Playing attacks before Bloodletting or Bash, missing the energy and Vulnerable multiplier.
counterfactual: Do not apply if Bloodletting HP cost would put you in lethal range or if enemy has Thorns/Reflect.

trigger: when facing Mawler and holding Unrelenting with other attacks in hand
lesson: Unrelenting first enables a free attack, maximizing damage output per energy by chaining into a 0-cost attack before spending energy on other cards.
recommendation: Play Unrelenting as the first attack to make the next attack free, then follow with a high-damage or utility attack (e.g., Pillage) before spending remaining energy on other attacks.
anti_pattern: Playing Unrelenting later in the turn or after other attacks wastes its free-attack benefit.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the free attack would be a low-value card (e.g., a basic Strike) and you have better energy-efficient plays.

trigger: when Mawler is not attacking (e.g., buffing) and you have self-damage cards like Breakthrough
lesson: Against Mawler during non-attack turns, safely use self-damage cards like Breakthrough to accelerate damage without needing block, as the HP loss is minimal compared to the damage dealt.
recommendation: Play Breakthrough aggressively when Mawler is not attacking to reduce its HP quickly, accepting the 1 HP loss per use.
anti_pattern: Hesitating to play Breakthrough on non-attack turns due to HP loss, missing free damage windows.
counterfactual: Avoid if your HP is critically low (e.g., below 10) or if Mawler's next attack would be lethal.

trigger: enemy HP is low enough to be lethal with any attack
lesson: When enemy HP is within lethal range of any attack, prioritize the cheapest attack to secure the kill and avoid unnecessary damage.
recommendation: If any attack in hand can kill the enemy, play the cheapest one (lowest energy cost) to end the fight safely.
anti_pattern: Playing a more expensive or unnecessary card when a cheap lethal is available, risking wasted energy or missing lethal due to misordering.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy has block or intangible that could prevent lethal.

trigger: enemy has Buff intent and no incoming damage this turn
lesson: Prioritize playing scaling powers (Inflame, Feel No Pain) and draw-efficient attacks (Pillage) over basic Strikes when enemy is not attacking, to set up future turns.
recommendation: On safe turns, play powers first to scale, then use draw attacks to cycle deck, then dump remaining energy into Strikes.
anti_pattern: Playing Strikes before powers on a safe turn, missing the opportunity to scale without penalty.
counterfactual: If enemy is attacking this turn and you lack sufficient block, prioritize defense over scaling.

trigger: enemy HP is low enough to kill this turn and you have Bloodletting in hand
lesson: Use Bloodletting to generate extra energy for a lethal burst turn, accepting the 3 HP loss to avoid incoming damage next turn.
recommendation: Calculate if Bloodletting + remaining energy enables lethal; if yes, play Bloodletting first to fuel the kill sequence.
anti_pattern: Ending turn without using Bloodletting when it would enable lethal, letting the enemy attack again.
counterfactual: If you cannot kill this turn even with Bloodletting, or if the 3 HP loss would put you in lethal range, skip it.

trigger: when enemy is at low HP and will deal lethal or high damage next turn
lesson: Prioritize lethal damage over self-damage from Breakthrough when the HP cost is negligible relative to the damage avoided.
recommendation: If Breakthrough can kill the enemy this turn and the self-damage is small (e.g., 1 HP), play it to end combat immediately and avoid incoming damage.
anti_pattern: Hesitating to use self-damage cards like Breakthrough for lethal when the HP loss is trivial.
counterfactual: Do not apply if the self-damage would put you in lethal range or if the enemy has a weak attack that turn.

trigger: when facing Vantom with Slippery active and have free attacks or zero-cost attacks in hand
lesson: Against Vantom's Slippery, prioritize playing free or zero-cost attacks first to chip away Slippery charges before committing energy-costing attacks, maximizing damage efficiency.
recommendation: Play Breakthrough, free attacks, or zero-cost attacks before playing energy-costing attacks to reduce Slippery charges and enable full damage from subsequent attacks.
anti_pattern: Playing energy-costing attacks first while Slippery is active, wasting energy on reduced damage.
counterfactual: Not applicable if Slippery is not active or if you have attacks that ignore block.

trigger: when facing Vantom with high HP (above 75%) and enemy attack is small (7 damage)
lesson: Against Vantom with high HP, it is safe to take small damage (7) to set up scaling (Inflame) and cycle cards (Burning Pact) rather than blocking, as long-term value outweighs minor HP loss.
recommendation: Prioritize playing scaling cards like Inflame and card draw/cycle like Burning Pact over blocking when HP is high and enemy damage is low, to build advantage for the long fight.
anti_pattern: Wasting energy on block when HP is high and enemy damage is minimal, delaying scaling and card draw.
counterfactual: Not applicable if HP is low (below 50%) or enemy damage is high (above 15).

trigger: when facing Vantom with high HP and limited block value in hand
lesson: Against Vantom, taking small damage to save energy for next turn is often better than playing inefficient block cards, because block expires and Vantom's Slippery debuff reduces attack damage.
recommendation: If HP is high (above 75%) and you have no efficient block, consider ending turn to preserve energy for stronger plays next turn.
anti_pattern: Playing weak block cards just to avoid chip damage when HP is high and energy is scarce.
counterfactual: Do not apply if HP is low (below 30%) or if you have a high-value block card like Shrug It Off that also draws.

trigger: when you have Headbutt in hand and a useful card in discard pile
lesson: Headbutt can be used to set up a key card from discard on top of draw pile for next turn, even if it deals minimal damage.
recommendation: Play Headbutt to retrieve a high-impact card (e.g., Bash, Heavy Strike) from discard, especially if you have energy to spare and the damage is secondary.
anti_pattern: Holding Headbutt for later when you could immediately set up a strong next turn.
counterfactual: Do not use if the discard pile has no impactful card to retrieve, or if you need the energy for a more urgent play this turn.

trigger: when facing Vantom with Headbutt in hand and 2 energy available
lesson: Headbutt's primary value is deck manipulation, not damage or Slippery reduction. Using it to retrieve a key card from discard (e.g., Burning Pact for draw) can be more impactful than playing a Strike for marginal Slippery reduction.
recommendation: Prioritize using Headbutt to retrieve a high-value card from discard over playing it for damage or Slippery reduction, especially when energy is limited.
anti_pattern: Playing Headbutt for damage and Slippery reduction without considering the retrieval target, wasting its deck manipulation potential.
counterfactual: If the hand has no valuable card to retrieve from discard, or if Slippery reduction is critical to avoid lethal damage, then damage/Slippery reduction may take priority.

trigger: when Vantom has Slippery active (damage reduced to 1 for multiple hits)
lesson: When Slippery is active, prioritize playing cards that consume its charges efficiently: use multi-hit attacks or cards that provide utility (draw, energy) over single high-damage attacks. Ending turn to preserve hand is acceptable if no beneficial play exists.
recommendation: Play Pillage for chip damage and draw, then Unrelenting to set up a free next attack, then free attacks like Strike. Avoid Breakthrough if it costs HP for minimal gain.
anti_pattern: Playing high-cost attacks or Breakthrough for 1 damage when Slippery is active, wasting HP and energy.
counterfactual: Not applicable when Slippery is exhausted or enemy is not using it.

trigger: when at low HP (below 25%) and Vantom has Slippery active, with Bloodletting in hand
lesson: At low HP with Slippery active, use Bloodletting to gain energy for multiple attacks, but play Defend first to ensure survival against incoming damage. Sequence: Defend -> Bloodletting -> attacks.
recommendation: Play Defend first to gain block, then Bloodletting for energy, then use remaining energy on attacks that consume Slippery charges (Bash for Vulnerable, Headbutt for damage and deck manipulation).
anti_pattern: Playing Bloodletting first at low HP, risking lethal damage from enemy attack.
counterfactual: Not applicable if enemy is not attacking that turn or if you have sufficient HP buffer.

trigger: when Vantom has Slippery active and you have a low-damage attack that can consume it
lesson: Use a low-damage attack first to consume Slippery before playing a high-damage attack, even if the low-damage attack applies a debuff like Vulnerable.
recommendation: Order attacks to strip Slippery with the weakest hit first, then follow with the main damage card to maximize effective damage.
anti_pattern: Playing a high-damage attack first when Slippery is active, wasting most of its damage.
counterfactual: If the low-damage attack also has a critical debuff that must land before other effects, consider alternative sequencing.

trigger: when HP is below enemy's incoming attack damage and no block is available
lesson: Do not end turn if any action (including playing a self-damage card) could potentially reduce enemy damage output or increase block; ending turn is only safe when no alternative exists.
recommendation: Before ending turn with lethal incoming damage, check if any card in hand can generate block, apply weak, or kill the enemy, even if it costs HP or resources.
anti_pattern: Ending turn without exhausting all possible defensive or offensive options when facing lethal damage.
counterfactual: If no cards are in hand and no potions are available, ending turn is the only option.
